subject: Deal-tier surge protection runbook and approval flow
messages:
From: Elliot Rhodes <elliot@luminary.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Surge trigger and protection ask for committed pool

Soojin —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We’re getting internal pushback on committing a reserved pool without a clear playbook for GPU-price or capacity shocks. Specifically Luminary wants to see:

- a trigger definition (what spike or index moves start the protection)
- an operational runbook (who to call, fallback to burst/dedicated swaps)
- commercial protections (credit, temporary discount, or right to re-evaluate pricing if market GPU cost moves > X%)

Can Redwood provide a short runbook + approval matrix we can include in our SOW? We don’t need legal text — just the operations and commercial guardrails to present to finance.

I attached a short internal Luminary note for context.

Thanks,
Elliot Rhodes
Head of Infrastructure
Luminary AI

Attachment: Luminary_Risk_Request.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Rhodes <elliot@luminary.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Surge trigger and protection ask for committed pool

Team — forwarding Luminary's note. High priority: they want an operational + commercial runbook to include in the SOW. Can we draft a concise 1–2 page runbook with approval thresholds? Key constraints below:

- Customer wants clarity on what constitutes a "GPU cost shock" (they suggested >25% YoY spot/repurchase cost movement or supply-related capacity constraint for >14 days)
- They expect either a temporary credit, automatic discount step-down, or the ability to convert part of committed pool to burst with a pricing collar
- Any proposed commercial protection needs an internal approval ladder (AE -> RevOps -> Finance -> CRO) and an SLA fallback (route to alternate region or burst).

Marcus — can you start a sensitivity model and an ops runbook?
Neha — procurement/finance input on acceptable thresholds and what we can commit to (escrow, credits, capped adjustment).
Sean — flagging for final approval lane and any exec-level constraints.

I’ve attached a quick template: surge_runbook_draft_v0.1.pdf. I’ll iterate once you drop comments.

Thanks,
Soojin
Sr. Manager, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

Attachment: surge_runbook_draft_v0.1.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Surge trigger and protection ask for committed pool

Adding an initial sensitivity table and an ops sketch. High-level points:

- Trigger mechanics: define two independent triggers
  1) PRICE: moving average of vendor GPU cost or market index increases by >=20% over rolling 30 days
  2) CAPACITY: sustained region-level utilization >92% for 10 days causing unacceptable queuing

- Commercial levers (proposed, each mapped to approval tier):
  * Auto-credit (up to 10% monthly credit for the first 60 days) — RevOps approval
  * Temporary discount corridor: if PRICE trigger hits, discount of up to 15% on new tokens for affected tier — Finance + CRO signoff
  * Convert portion of reserved pool to burst with a capped premium (max +25%) for up to 90 days — Sales + Ops approval (requires capacity matrix mapping)

- Ops runbook (concise):
  1) Alert from monitoring -> Ops on-call pages SRE + Account AE
  2) AE opens a risk ticket with RevOps (include deal id DL-2026-1173)
  3) RevOps runs sensitivity model (attached) and recommends commercial remedy within 48 hours
  4) If commercial remedy requires discount >10% or credit >10%/month, escalate to Finance + CRO for approval

I attached a simple model and flagged cells for incremental cost impact at 10/15/25% GPU cost moves. Marcus

Attachment: pricing_sensitivity_model.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Surge trigger and protection ask for committed pool

Good draft — a few commercial guardrails from procurement perspective:

- Thresholds: procurement teams rarely accept open-ended index clauses. Recommend we limit automatic commercial adjustments to 1 discrete window per 12-month period unless market behavior is extreme (panel to review)
- Escrow: offer a capped escrow/credit pool (example: up to 12% of monthly committed spend held as contingency) that can be applied if the PRICE trigger fires. Release terms: prorated over next 6 months if unused.
- Review cadence: if trigger persists beyond 60 days, allow a formal re-price negotiation with 30-day notice, limited to a maximum of 20% adjustment in either direction and subject to exec approval.

Operational asks: condition any burst conversion on capacity availability guarantees in alternate regions and limit the conversion share to no more than 40% of committed pool to protect baseline utilization.

I'll annotate Marcus's spreadsheet with the procurement-friendly cells. If we provide the escrow option, legal will need a short clause; we should avoid long-term indexation.

-Neha
Head of Procurement Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Surge trigger and protection ask for committed pool

Thanks team — good work. Approve the proposed structure with these final constraints:

- Approve: PRICE trigger at 20% MA30 and CAPACITY trigger as Marcus proposed.
- Approve: auto-credit up to 8% monthly for up to 60 days before escalation to Finance for higher credit/discounts.
- Approve: one escrow event per 12 months up to 10% of committed monthly spend, prorated recovery over 6 months.
- Approve: burst conversion as temporary remediation but cap at 35% of pool and require Ops confirmation of cross-region capacity.

Next steps:
- Soojin: incorporate these numbers into the runbook and send a clean 2-page PDF to Luminary by EOD Friday.
- Marcus: finalize your spreadsheet with the approved thresholds and upload to the deal record.
- Neha: coordinate with Legal to draft a short SOW clause (we'll keep indexation out of the contract; use escrow + single re-price window).

If Luminary pushes for a larger safety net, escalate to me and I’ll take to CRO.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
